meta.title: Beyond Data — tool logic
meta.scale: 100 arithmetic/physics · 90 regulation, tariff or standard read directly · 80 government dataset or statistic · 70 peer-reviewed coefficient transferred from another context · 60 derived with stated assumption · 50 operator or industry claim · 40 proxy · 20 judged · 0 gap
meta.rule: A quantity's confidence is the lowest of its inputs; a condition's is the lowest of its quantities; a match fails at its weakest link; burdens are recorded beside, never netted.

verdict_states.label: works
verdict_states.means: every condition for the match passes

verdict_states.label: works with a change
verdict_states.means: at least one condition passes only if a named change is made; the blocker is named

verdict_states.label: doesn't work
verdict_states.means: a condition fails and no change within the match removes it; the blocker is named

verdict_states.label: not applicable or declined
verdict_states.means: the condition does not bear on this match, or the receiver has said no — a valid answer, not a failure

verdict_states.label: cannot judge
verdict_states.means: a figure the condition needs is missing; the tool names which (operator floor price, parcel MW headroom, BC marginal factor, per-activity intensity)

verdict_states.label: not judged
verdict_states.means: the run has not reached this condition yet

nodes.name: Heat-pump COP (Lorenz)
nodes.formula: COP = η × T_lm,sink ÷ (T_lm,sink − T_lm,source), log-mean temperatures on both sides (sink supply/return; source in/out); η 0.40–0.50 for built systems (calibrated 13 Oct 2026), 0.50–0.60 upper bound
nodes.coef: checks: ~3 at 20→75 °C; 4.5–5.0 Odense; DEA Aug 2026 waste-heat heat pumps, annual average COP to 70 °C forward / 35 °C return: 3.1 at 1 MW (source 13→8 °C), 3.6 at 3 MW (15→8 °C), 4.7 at 10 MW (27→15 °C); air-source 3 MW 2.8; CALIBRATION 13 Oct 2026 (calibrate.py; sources/13): full Lorenz with η 0.50 gives 4.56 for Odense (27→15 / 40→75 °C) against realised 4.5 (2020) and 4.2 all-in (2021–22, η 0.49 / 0.46); Telia Helsinki snapshot 3.9 at 20/32 → ~80 °C implies η 0.39; Université Laval ~7 at ~15 → 40 °C implies η 0.53; ReUseHeat design 3.6 and Bahnhof simulation 3.7 imply 0.37 / 0.43. The simplified form used in the first attempt (sink supply ÷ (sink supply − source out)) under-predicts at large lifts (3.0–3.6 for Odense) and is retired
nodes.status: calibrated on six cases: η 0.39–0.53 built/operating

nodes.name: Heat captured at the boundary (E_reuse)
nodes.formula: E_reuse = heat_rejected × liquid_capture, measured at the data-centre boundary by flow × ΔT before any heat pump (ISO/IEC 30134-6 cl.5–6; EU Reg. 2024/1364 Annex II 1(j))
nodes.coef: This is the figure a data centre may report as reused energy and the numerator of ERF; the network-side figure after the heat pump (what Stockholm Exergi and Fjernvarme Fyn meter and bill, and what Danish tax law meters "ved udgang fra varmepumpe" with 3 × electricity deducted) is heat_delivered, not E_reuse. The two differ by COP ÷ (COP − 1) ≈ 1.3 at COP 4.2. Published "heat delivered" figures must be labelled by which boundary they use; where the source does not say, mark unknown.

source_roles.term: Danish tax metering at heat-pump outlet, 3 × electricity deducted

Alberta (Guide to Groundwater Authorization 2023 §6.2): open loop with no water loss and return to the same water body = Water Act "activity" → approval; different water body or any loss → licence; closed loop → none. Flow tier for the aquifer test: Q(m³/day) = heat_kW ÷ (1.16 × ΔT) × 24; a 1 MW loop at ΔT 5 K ≈ 4,100 m³/day → top tier
nodes.coef: Alberta EPA fact sheet, Ground Source Heat Exchange Systems (8 Oct 2025; 2024 edition identical on these points): open-loop systems "are regulated through a Water Act authorization" obtained before construction; application must assess the aquifer's capability to circulate the required quantity continuously, effects on groundwater quantity, temperature and quality, and on household, agricultural and existing licence holders; complex systems need an APEGA groundwater specialist report per the Guide to Groundwater Authorization; water in an open loop cannot be used for another purpose or temporarily discharged; open-loop wells drilled by a Class A driller, return through a separate return well; horizontal closed loop above the water table and vertical closed loop above the base of groundwater protection need no Water Act authorization (Class F installer); below the base of groundwater protection the AER regulates under the Geothermal Resource Development Act; applications via DRAS. Directive (11 Dec 2018) sets the construction standards; Guide App. 2 aquifer-test tiers by daily pumping rate: ≤10 m³/day 2+2 h, no observation well, no APEGA report (§2.2); 10–35 m³/day 24+24 h, 0–1 obs well; 35–65 m³/day 24+24 h, 1; 65–265 m³/day 48+48 h, 1–2; >265 m³/day 72+72 h, 1–2 obs wells, full §2 report by an APEGA groundwater practitioner; maximum daily rate = lesser of test rate and Q20 (20-year sustainable yield); CSA C448 referenced for installation; temporary discharge needs the director's authorisation

Alberta: approval vs licence; aquifer test tiers
Alberta fact sheet: authorization before construction

conditions.heading: 11 Add-ons
conditions.name: Water reuse is allowed for this source and use
conditions.test: city × source (rain, reclaimed, greywater, blackwater) × use (cooling make-up) is permitted
conditions.note: Vancouver 2019 by-law: rainwater and clear-water waste may supply cooling-tower make-up; greywater and blackwater may not be collected (Art. 2.7.1.2); the 2025 by-law adds residential greywater systems (NSF 350) — non-residential status to confirm. Alberta: single-property reuse limited to toilets and subsurface irrigation (P-17-01, archived), other uses by variance; Alberta Health 2021 lists cooling towers with treatment targets. Taking someone else's treated wastewater needs Water Act authorisation in Alberta and falls under the Municipal Wastewater Regulation in BC.

conditions.heading: 11 Add-ons
conditions.name: Solar fits the generation rules
conditions.test: size and export within the provincial programme
conditions.note: BC Hydro RS 2289 (from 1 Jul 2026): up to 100 kW AC, exports credited 10 ¢/kWh; larger needs interconnection study. Alberta: micro-generation ≤ 5 MW and ≤ the site's annual use, retail credit under 150 kW, pool price above.

conditions.heading: 11 Add-ons
conditions.name: There is ground for a borefield
conditions.test: borefield area ≤ land available on or next to the parcel (parking, parks, streets)
conditions.note: ≈2 ha per MW rejected to ground alone; Alberta setbacks 1 m from buildings, 3 m from property lines, 15 m from water wells; BC closed-loop wells need a registered driller and a construction report; boreholes under streets or parks need City agreement (rules not found).

conditions.heading: 11 Add-ons
conditions.name: The heat is hot enough to make cooling
conditions.test: heat temperature ≥ the absorption chiller's minimum
conditions.note: Air-cooled heat cannot drive absorption cooling; liquid-cooled heat can only with a heat-pump lift or a low-COP two-stage machine.

conditions.heading: 11 Add-ons
conditions.name: Battery storage meets fire rules on an urban site
conditions.test: code path and separation for a battery system are confirmed
conditions.note: Whether NFPA 855 is referenced by the BC or Alberta building and fire codes was not confirmed; Technical Safety BC withdrew its storage bulletin in March 2025.
